newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan police say boy killed; protests broken up.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan police say boy killed; protests broken up.

text.p: Police said a boy was killed in the Kenyan town of Thika on Monday but denied any involvement as riot police broke up protests in the capital and several other towns.
Police spokesman Assistant Commissioner Peter Kimanthi said the body of the boy was brought to a road in the Majengo area of Thika and an investigation was under way to determine how he was killed.
Kenyan journalists said they had received and were checking reports from Thika that the schoolboy was shot dead at Kairi secondary school in Thika and two others were seriously wounded.

"Young people brought the body of the young man to the road in Majengo and it was taken to hospital. We don't know what caused the death of this person but we did not police Majengo," Kimanthi told Reuters.
"We have launched an investigation into how he was killed."

Kimanthi said demonstrators demanding constitutional reforms burned kiosks in Thika but police had moved in and controlled the situation. He also reported some disturbances in the nearby town of Nyahururu and in the western Kenyan town of Kisumu.

Riot police and paramilitary General Service Unit personnel broke up demonstrations in the capital Nairobi, badly beating people on the streets with batons even after they surrendered, witnesses said.
